name: National Health Policy, 2017
change: Reoriented the public health system towards preventive and promotive care, expanded primary healthcare coverage, and set targets for reducing maternal and infant mortality.
impact: Strengthens overall healthcare delivery and long-term public health outcomes, but depends heavily on state-level implementation and funding.

name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, 2018
change: Provides health insurance coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization for economically vulnerable populations.
impact: Improves access to hospital care and reduces out-of-pocket expenses, though hospital capacity and fraud control remain concerns.

name: National Digital Health Mission, 2020
change: Introduced digital health IDs, electronic health records, and integrated health data systems for seamless healthcare delivery.
impact: Enhances efficiency and continuity of care through data integration. Raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity.

name: Jan Aushadhi Scheme Expansion, 2015
change: Expansion of government-supported stores providing low-cost generic medicines across the country.
impact: Reduces cost burden on patients and improves access to essential medicines, especially for low-income groups.

name: National Health Mission, 2013
change: Integrated rural and urban health missions to strengthen primary healthcare infrastructure, maternal health services, and disease control programs.
impact: Improves accessibility of healthcare in underserved areas, though quality and staffing challenges persist.

name: PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission, 2021
change: Focuses on strengthening health infrastructure including critical care units, labs, and disease surveillance systems.
impact: Enhances preparedness for pandemics and improves healthcare capacity nationwide.

name: National Telemedicine Guidelines, 2020
change: Legalized and standardized telemedicine practices, allowing remote consultation between doctors and patients using digital platforms.
impact: Improves access to healthcare in remote areas and reduces hospital load. Requires digital literacy and internet access.

name: Universal Immunization Programme Expansion, 2014
change: Expanded vaccine coverage to include additional diseases and increased focus on nationwide immunization drives.
impact: Reduces child mortality and controls preventable diseases. Requires continuous awareness and logistical support.

name: National Mental Health Programme Strengthening, 2014
change: Expansion of mental health services, awareness programs, and integration into primary healthcare systems.
impact: Improves recognition and treatment of mental health issues. Still faces stigma and shortage of professionals.

name: eSanjeevani Telehealth Platform, 2020
change: Government-supported telemedicine platform providing online doctor consultations across India.
impact: Increases accessibility to medical advice and reduces travel burden for patients, especially in rural regions.
